name: George W. Fitzgerald
role: Keeper of the Hotel de Mores; builder of a new Medora hotel
bio: George Fitzgerald kept the Hotel de Mores in Medora, where in 1884 he gave dances, lent his room to the April Republican convention, hosted a Catholic mass in August, and served as treasurer of the Little Missouri school fund. In July 1884 his appearance scared off three strangers who seemed ready to steal horses tied outside the hotel. From late 1884 he built a new hotel, with brick plans drawn by Peter Book and Henry Brick; the plastering and inside work were done by February 1885, and in April 1886 the paper said he meant to open it soon. In 1885 he was subpoenaed as a witness in William Roberts' horse-theft case at Miles City, and in December he settled a case against Gregor Lang when Lang bought his brand.
